title: NEET-UG may shift from pen-and-paper to online mode as Centre works on national CBT infrastructure
text: NEET-UG could shift from pen-and-paper to computer-based testing as the Centre prepares a national CBT framework, with rural access, infrastructure and equity among candidates being considered before a final decision. The Ministry of Education is working on a national-level Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy that could pave the way for NEET-UG to move from its existing pen-and-paper format to an online examination system according to media reports. The proposed shift is being examined as part of the broader effort to strengthen Indiaâs public examination system following the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. However, the government is expected to take a final decision only after receiving the recommendations of the high-level task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani . Centre plans national CBT infrastructure for entrance exams A senior Ministry of Education official told PTI that the government is preparing a national examination-grade CBT infrastructure framework. The proposed system is intended to address the uneven availability of suitable test centres across the country, establish common technical standards, and make it possible to shift examinations currently held in pen-and-paper format to computer-based testing. The strategy is also being considered through a multi-model sourcing approach, under which different mechanisms could potentially be used to create and expand examination infrastructure. The move is not limited to NEET-UG. Once the required infrastructure is established, the broader objective is to facilitate the migration of more entrance examinations to the online mode. Several major examinations conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), including JEE Main, CUET-UG, CUET-PG, UGC-NET and CSIR-UGC-NET, are already conducted in CBT mode. NEET-UG remains one of the major exceptions, with candidates currently taking the examination using pen and paper. NEET online shift to factor in rural and low-connectivity areas Moving an examination as large as NEET-UG to CBT would require more than simply setting up additional computer centres. The government is examining how the transition would affect candidates in rural and remote areas, particularly those living in districts with limited connectivity and access to examination infrastructure. The Ministry official said the proposed NEET transition plan is examining the sequencing of the shift, infrastructure requirements, and its implications for equity among candidates, including rural candidates and women. This aspect assumes importance because NEET-UG is taken by candidates from across the country, including students from areas where access to reliable digital infrastructure may be limited. The government is therefore looking at the infrastructure requirements before making a final decision on the mode of the examination. Nandan Nilekani-led task force report awaited The proposed changes are also linked to the wider examination reforms being considered by the Centre. The NEET-UG paper leak controversy triggered widespread protests and prompted the government to examine vulnerabilities in the country's examination system. Prime Minister Narendra Modi subsequently announced a high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani to recommend measures to strengthen and secure public examinations. The task force's recommendations are still awaited. According to the Ministry official, the final approach to shifting NEET-UG to CBT will take into account the panel's recommendations as well as consultations with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Medical Commission. The NTA is separately undergoing an overhaul as the government reviews the way major entrance and eligibility examinations are conducted. NEET-UG is taken by nearly 25 lakh candidates The scale of NEET-UG makes the proposed transition particularly challenging. Nearly 25 lakh candidates appear for the examination every year, making it one of India's largest undergraduate entrance tests. NEET scores are used for admission to MBBS programmes as well as undergraduate courses in dentistry, Ayurveda, Unani, and Siddha. There are around 1.08 lakh MBBS seats in the country, including approximately 56,000 seats in government medical colleges and around 52,000 in private institutions. A shift to CBT would therefore require a large and geographically distributed network of examination centres capable of handling the candidate volume while maintaining uniform examination conditions. NEET CBT proposal gains momentum after paper leak The possibility of conducting NEET-UG online is not new. The proposal has been discussed at various points in the past, but the recent examination controversy has given fresh momentum to the idea. For the government, the immediate task is to determine whether the country has, or can build, the infrastructure needed for such a large-scale transition without creating new disadvantages for candidates. For now, NEET-UG continues to remain a pen-and-paper examination. The Centre is working on the infrastructure framework, while the final decision on the transition to CBT is expected after the Nilekani-led task force submits its recommendations and consultations with the health authorities are completed. title: NEET-UG to shift online? Centre works on nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy
text: NEET-UG may shift online as Centre develops nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy NEW DELHI: The ministry of education is developing a nationwide Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy to enable the transition of NEET from its current pen-and-paper format to an online examination, officials said. While NEET has so far been conducted in pen-and-paper mode, the National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts several other examinations, including JEE-Main, Common University Entrance Test (CUET)-UG and PG, UGC-NET and CSIR UGC-NET, in computer-based mode. Once the infrastructure strategy is in place, the plan is to shift all entrance examinations to the online mode. "A national examination-grade Computer-Based Testing infrastructure strategy is being formulated to close the geographic gap in test-centre availability, standardise centre-level examination-grade specifications and to permit the migration to CBT from the pen-and-paper mode examinations. The strategy is under active consideration based on a multi-model sourcing architecture," a senior Ministry of Education official was quoted as saying by PTI. The move comes amid an ongoing overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA), the nodal autonomous body responsible for conducting NEET-UG and other entrance examinations for higher educational institutions. "The possible migration of NEET (UG) from the pen-and-paper mode to CBT, including the design of the transition, the sequencing, the infrastructure prerequisites, and the equity implications for rural, women and low-connectivity-district candidates, is being worked upon. However, the recommendations of the High-Level Task Force on exam reforms in structured consultation and concurrence of the Health Ministry and National Medical Commission, are awaited," the official said. Following the NEET paper leak earlier this year, the Centre announced that the medical entrance examination would be conducted in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from next year. Officials aware of the development said the plan is under active consideration, but a final decision will be taken only after the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force set up to overhaul Indiaâs public examination system is received. The leak of the NEET-UG medical entrance examination paper earlier this year triggered nationwide student protests and led to the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. A day after Pradhanâs resignation, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the formation of a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms aimed at making the examination system leakproof. title: NEET-UG paper leak: NTA withholds result of Latur coaching centre owner's son, bars him from exam for 2 years
text: Latur coaching centre owner, Shivraj Motegaonkar The National Testing Agency (NTA) has debarred Aditya Motegaonkar, son of paper leak accused Shivraj Motegaonkar, from appearing for the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, for two years. His result for the examination conducted earlier this year has been withheld, and he has been declared ineligible for NEET-UG 2027, according to an NTA communication. Shivraj Motegaonkar, who runs a coaching centre in Latur, was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in connection with this year's NEET-UG paper leak case. He is currently in judicial custody. Watch NEET Paper Leak Traced To Contracted Paper Setters, Charge Sheet Likely This Month | Watch What the CBI alleges According to the CBI, Shivraj Motegaonkar paid Rs 5 lakh to P V Kulkarni to procure chemistry questions. Kulkarni was on the NTA panel that set the questions for the examination. The agency has further alleged that Aditya Motegaonkar attended Kulkarni's coaching classes, where the questions were provided. How the NTA acted The NTA cancelled the NEET-UG held on May 3 on May 12, following allegations of a paper leak. The examination was meant for admissions to medical courses. A re-examination was conducted on June 21. After the retest, the NTA placed Aditya Motegaonkar's result on hold and asked him to explain the alleged irregularities. The candidate's response In his reply, Aditya Motegaonkar denied having used unfair means during the examination. He also argued that the notice issued to him related to alleged irregularities in the May 3 examination. He questioned why his result in the retest had been withheld. The NTA has since withheld his result and imposed the two-year debarment. The CBI last month submitted its final report before the designated fast-track court in Delhi. The court is dealing with criminal cases arising from paper leaks as well as the use of other unfair means in public examinations. NEET-UG is conducted by the NTA for medical aspirants. title: NTA new office under review: Higher Education Secretary checks security, infrastructure ahead of upcoming exams
text: Higher Education Secretary Deepti Gaur Mukherjee reviews the NTAâs new Minto Road office as the agency strengthens infrastructure, access controls and confidential examination safeguards ahead of upcoming tests. Higher Education Secretary Deepti Gaur Mukherjee on Saturday reviewed the infrastructure and administrative arrangements at the National Testing Agencyâs (NTA) newly relocated office in New Delhi, with the government focusing on strengthening examination-related operations ahead of upcoming tests. The review comes weeks after the NTA shifted its confidential and sensitive operations from its previous Okhla premises to a new government facility on Minto Road amid heightened scrutiny over examination security and the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. The Ministry of Education said Mukherjee interacted with senior NTA officials and inspected the operational facilities during her visit. The review was aimed at ensuring that the agency has the necessary infrastructure and administrative systems in place for the smooth conduct of forthcoming examinations. Higher Education Secretary reviews new NTA premises According to the Ministry of Education, Mukherjee carried out a comprehensive assessment of the new infrastructure and administrative setup during her visit. âSecretary, Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Smt. Deepti Gaur Mukherjee visited the new NTA office,â the ministry said in a post on X. It added that she interacted with senior officials, inspected operational facilities and reviewed the arrangements to ensure the seamless conduct of upcoming examinations. The visit assumes importance as the testing agency prepares to conduct several major national-level examinations, including tests such as JEE Main, NEET-UG, CUET and UGC-NET. NTA shifts operations from Okhla to Minto Road The NTA has moved its headquarters from Okhla to the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road in central New Delhi. The new facility has been allotted more than 55,000 square feet of space, covering the fifth floor and portions of the fourth and sixth floors of the building. The relocation was ordered after a review of the agency's examination systems and security arrangements. In August, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi directed the NTA to shift to the new premises and strengthen security infrastructure. The agency subsequently announced a broader restructuring of its examination operations. The NTA had earlier operated from its office in Okhla. Its shift to a government premises is part of the measures being undertaken to strengthen the handling of confidential examination material and tighten access to sensitive operations. CISF deployed at confidential areas Security arrangements at the new premises have also been strengthened. The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) has deployed 39 personnel at the facility to regulate access to confidential areas and conduct security screening. According to officials cited by PTI, CISF personnel are stationed at entry and exit points and are responsible for access control, frisking and baggage screening. X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors are also part of the security arrangements. Confidential areas have been separately demarcated, with movement and operations within these sections subject to tighter monitoring. The Centre has also been working on strengthened security protocols for the facility. Air-gapped systems, restricted access part of security overhaul The physical relocation is accompanied by tighter controls over digital and confidential operations. The new setup includes secluded rooms for sensitive work, air-gapped systems and mandatory device-deposit protocols intended to limit unauthorised access to examination-related information. The Centre has also said that standard operating procedures covering key NTA processes are being implemented across the examination cycle. Security arrangements for confidential operations have been consolidated as part of the agency's broader restructuring. The NTA has further strengthened its information-security structure, with the Centre stating that a dedicated Chief Information Security Officer has been designated and recruitment for additional information-security expertise is under way. NEET paper leak brought NTA's examination systems under scrutiny The latest security measures follow intense scrutiny of the NTA after the NEET-UG paper leak controversy. The issue triggered protests by students and raised questions over the agency's examination and confidentiality protocols. The CBI's investigation into the leak highlighted specific shortcomings in the handling of confidential material. According to the chargesheet, subject experts accused of being involved in the leak were not checked or frisked while entering or leaving the confidential section of the NTA's earlier office. The investigation also pointed to the absence of a dedicated control room for monitoring live CCTV feeds. The controversy subsequently prompted the government to initiate a wider examination-system overhaul. The Centre has been examining changes involving infrastructure, staffing, security protocols and the handling of question papers. NTA strengthens examination team and question-paper checks Alongside the office relocation, the NTA has begun restructuring its examination team. In August, the agency announced that around 600 experts associated with question-paper setting were being removed and that new experts would be brought into the system. The agency has also proposed a four-tier question-paper checking mechanism, while plans were announced to induct additional officials to strengthen its examination operations. The measures are being implemented as the NTA seeks to tighten its examination infrastructure and processes before the next round of major national-level tests. With the new premises now operational and additional physical and digital safeguards being put in place, Saturday's review by the Higher Education Secretary marks another step in the government's ongoing monitoring of the agency's preparedness for upcoming examinations. title: NEET leak fallout: CISF to guard NTAâs confidential exam areas
text: (Representative image): CISF will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs). NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has tightened security around its examination work with 39 CISF personnel deployed at its New Delhi office. The force will monitor confidential areas, control access and screen staff and visitors. The move follows repeated questions over paper leaks and administrative lapses, including the handling of sensitive examination material. The CISF personnel have been deployed at entry and exit points of the confidential areas at the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. They will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs). The NTA has also demarcated confidential areas within its new premises. Movement and operations in these areas will be closely monitored as part of efforts to prevent unauthorised access to examination material. "Confidential areas have been demarcated in the building where the movement and operations will be strictly monitored to ensure that a foolproof system is in place. The Home Ministry has approved Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) security cover for the premises," a senior official said. NTA shifts sensitive operations to new office The security measures come after the NTA moved its confidential and sensitive operations from its earlier office in Okhla to a new facility on Minto Road. "A dedicated over 55,000 square feet office space has been allotted in the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. The fifth floor and parts of the fourth and sixth floors of the said building have been allotted to the National Testing Agency. Confidential and sensitive operations have been shifted in the last one month to the newly allotted building," the official said. Other parts of the Government of India Press Building are already protected by the CISF. The NTA will now have a dedicated security arrangement for its examination-related confidential areas. The agency's new security framework also includes tighter monitoring of examination-critical technology systems. The NTA is working on strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage. "Arrangements are being made in mission mode for establishing strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage for all examination-critical workloads." Cybersecurity measures being strengthened The NTA is also reviewing the security of systems used throughout the examination cycle. These include candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing, OMR processing, result systems and other examination-supporting infrastructure. "Running security readiness reviews of all examination-supporting systems before each examination cycle in coordination with NTA's technology function and coordinating with NTA's test-security function on the technical security of examination day workflows -- including biometric authentication, face-matching, CCTV systems and live monitoring infrastructure -- are among the action items being worked upon," the official said. The agency is also preparing an examination-specific cyber-incident response system. It plans to have enhanced security operations centre monitoring and rapid-response capabilities on examination days. The NTA has designated a dedicated chief information security officer (CISO) to oversee information security. "The position of general manager and CISO has been advertised, and the selection process is at an advanced stage. Independent third-party cyber-security audits by CERT-In and C-DAC empanelled agencies continue to be undertaken," the official said. Paper leak exposed gaps in confidential section The latest security measures follow the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak, which triggered nationwide student protests and brought scrutiny on the NTA's examination processes. A CBI chargesheet identified three subject experts as the primary sources of the leaked paper. According to the chargesheet, experts entering the NTA's confidential section were not checked or frisked during entry or exit. The experts were allegedly able to take briefs from the question papers on small chits made from plain sheets provided to them for rough work and translation. The CBI also noted that the NTA did not have a dedicated CCTV live-feed monitoring control room in its Delhi office. This meant the activities of the three accused experts went unnoticed. The NTA was established in 2017 under the Ministry of Education to conduct fair, transparent and standardised examinations. Earlier reforms and fresh scrutiny The 2024 NEET paper leak had also led to the setting up of a high-level committee headed by former ISRO chairman K Radhakrishnan. The panel recommended stronger security controls across the examination process. Its recommendations covered question paper systems, candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing platforms, OMR processing, normalisation engines and result systems. title: NEET paper leak row: SC judges to visit NTA office to inspect upgraded facilities
text: SC bench plans NTA visit to inspect upgraded examination system NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday highlighted the need to institutionally strengthen the examination system to prevent recurring NEET paper leaks and indicated that judges of the bench would personally visit the National Testing Agency (NTA) to examine its upgraded facilities. Justice Narasimha said the judges would visit the NTA office on Minto Road in Delhi to assess whether the system is functional and examine its manpower and other arrangements. Watch NEET Paper Leak Traced To Contracted Paper Setters, Charge Sheet Likely This Month | Watch Justice PS Narasimha told Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, that he and Justice Aradhe would like to visit the National Testing Agency's newly upgraded facility to examine its systems. âStrengthening the NTA's system institutionally is crucial to preventing recurring paper leaks. Merely immediate or temporary measures would not suffice. You must know that permanency of the entire system is key. There should be a permanent setup, permanent staff, permanent verticals. Very less deputation should be there. Only then a permanent structure will come up,â the bench told Mehta. At the outset, the Centre told the bench that the high-powered panel led by Nandan Nilekani, constituted to suggest structural reforms in NEET, has held extensive consultations and is likely to submit its first interim report by the end of this month. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said suggestions received from stakeholders had been placed before the panel, which also held consultations with members of an earlier committee headed by former ISRO chairman K Radhakrishnan. The bench directed the joint secretary of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), who is assisting the Nilekani panel, to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken so far. The bench told Mehta that the key issue was to institutionalise the entire process for conducting the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET). The Education Department has said that a new and upgraded system has been created. The bench noted that the Radhakrishnan committee had also recommended structural reforms, but said the key issue was their implementation. Mehta assured the bench that the Nilekani panel was examining all recommendations made by the Radhakrishnan committee, as well as suggestions from the petitioners and other stakeholders. âIt is the top most priority of the government. All necessary assistance will be provided,â Mehta told the bench, as cited by PTI. The bench directed that the affidavit filed by the NTA be uploaded on its website to enable people to submit their suggestions. It also asked the Centre to appoint a nodal counsel through whom people could submit their suggestions. On August 19, the Supreme Court, observing the need to institutionalise reforms in the NTA, had directed the Centre to inform it about the steps taken to implement the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan panel and the Nilekani committee. The seven-member Radhakrishnan Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Education following the NEET-UG 2024 paper leak to recommend reforms in the examination process, strengthen data security protocols, and review the structure and functioning of the NTA. title: NTA needs complete overhaul, permanent staff to ensure foolproof exams: ABVP
text: NTA needs complete overhaul, permanent staff to ensure foolproof exams: ABVP RSS' student wing ABVP has sought a complete overhaul of the National Testing Agency ( NTA ), saying the examination body needs permanent staff and a "foolproof" system to prevent paper leaks and ensure accountability. In an exclusive interview with PTI, Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) national general secretary Dr Virendra Singh Solanki said the NTA requires several reforms, including reducing outsourcing, strengthening the paper-setting process and fixing accountability throughout the examination cycle. "The NTA requires a complete overhaul. There are many reforms that are required in the NTA. The NTA needs permanent staff. A lot of work is outsourced. The system of paper setters also needs to be made foolproof," he said. "From the allocation of the examination -- from the day the examination is announced, to its conduct and finally the declaration of results -- the entire process needs to be made foolproof," he stressed. "There should be people permanently responsible for these processes within the NTA, so that they remain accountable. That would significantly reduce the chances of compromise," Solanki said. "So I think reforms in the NTA are extremely necessary. If the body needs to be expanded, that should also be done," he added. NTA has been in the eye of a storm following the cancellation of the NEET-UG 2026 exams and irregularities in the UGC-NET exam. Solanki also said ABVP wants NEET-UG to be conducted twice a year and in computer-based test (CBT) mode, saying the model would reduce the risk of paper leaks while giving students another opportunity to perform well. "It will definitely reduce the risk and it will be very beneficial for students," he said. "Students will have two options. Many times, students preparing for medical examinations are unable to perform well due to personal reasons, or despite preparing well, their examination does not go as expected. If the exam is conducted twice, they will have another chance if they do not perform well the first time. "I also think this will significantly reduce the instances of students suffering mental distress or attempting suicide, because they will have another opportunity," he said. On the logistical challenges of conducting a CBT examination for around 12-13 lakh students, Solanki said the test could be held in multiple slots and centres. "Having that many computers available simultaneously and conducting the exam in a single slot is not possible. But I think it can be conducted in multiple slots, as is done for IIT examinations, and at different centres," he said. Asked about students in rural areas, Solanki said mock tests and training could familiarise them with CBT examinations and existing computer facilities in schools could be used. "Today, there is an education infrastructure across the country. Schools have computer classes, and these can be used to provide such facilities to students in remote areas. "Videos of mock tests can also be made available to students through YouTube and other digital platforms. There can be multiple ways to overcome this challenge and ultimately conduct the examination." "I think having the examination twice a year and conducting it in CBT mode would definitely be a major reform for NEET-UG students," he said. "When we imagine India in 2047 as a country where education is accessible, affordable and quality-oriented, and examinations are corruption-free and paper-leak-free, this could prove to be a major reform in that direction," he added. Solanki also called for strengthening the NTA's grievance redressal mechanism, particularly in view of concerns raised by students over answer keys and examination-related issues. "We want reforms because over the last two-three years there have been repeated incidents of paper leaks. Even after taking the examination, students remain doubtful about their answer keys. They may have certain concerns or issues, but they do not always receive proper responses from the grievance cell." "I think the NTA's grievance redressal mechanism needs to be developed properly so that no student is left with doubts. Students should be able to directly raise their questions and receive answers. "These are two reforms that are required, and we have already raised them," he said. On medical education, Solanki said requirements are varied for NEET, MBBS and postgraduate students and flagged pressure faced by MBBS students in the final year. "If we talk about MBBS students, there has already been a curriculum reform. The competency-based curriculum has been introduced, which is good. But in the final year of MBBS, all the clinical subjects have been brought together. "This creates a certain amount of pressure on students. Since they study clinical subjects gradually from the second year through the final year, there is considerable pressure when all of them come together in the final year.Something needs to be done to reduce that pressure," he said. Solanki also called for greater focus on the quality of internships, saying students should get adequate practical exposure. "Another issue is internships. Students need to take internships seriously, and the institutions conducting internships also need to ensure proper learning. "In some places, students are engaged in tasks that do not have much educational value -- filling files, making photocopies, accompanying patients for investigations and so on. This affects their productivity and the quality of their learning. "Some institutions do provide very good learning opportunities, but institutions need to think in this direction, and students also need to take internships seriously," he said. He said students often move towards postgraduate preparation during internships without getting enough opportunity to apply their MBBS learning in clinical settings. "During internships, students often move directly towards PG preparation and do not get the opportunity to practically learn what they studied during MBBS. They may not see enough patients in OPDs, observe procedures in OTs or assist in surgeries. "Instead, they directly move towards theoretical PG preparation. "I think students also need to think about this and give adequate importance to practical learning during their internships," Solanki said. Get the latest Education News and Live updates. title: NEET-UG paper leak case: Charges framed against 52 accused
text: CBI Patna : The NEET-UG 2024 paper leak case moved to the trial stage nearly two-and-a-half years after the examination with a special CBI court in Patna framing charges against 52 accused on Thursday. Special Judge Mohammad Rustam of CBI Court-II directed the prosecution to begin producing witnesses and documentary evidence from Oct 1. The CBI had filed a chargesheet against 54 accused, but proceedings against two were separated. The agency also did not chargesheet Sanjeev Kumar alias Sanjeev Mukhiya alias Lutan after failing to find evidence against him. Special Public Prosecutor Satyajit appeared for the CBI. The case came to light on May 5, 2024, when Shastrinagar police in Patna received information about a suspected paper leak network. Police intercepted a car carrying Sikandar Yadavendu, Akhilesh Kumar and Bittu Kumar and recovered photocopies of admit cards of several examinees and two mobile phones from Yadavendu. During questioning, investigators learnt about the alleged supply of question papers to candidates. Police then detained a candidate at DAV School, Punaichak, who said the paper had been provided to him at Learn Boys School and Learn Play School in Ramkrishna Nagar. The investigation also traced the alleged leak to the Oasis School examination centre in Hazaribagh, Jharkhand. According to the report, the paper was taken from the centreâs strongroom around 8.02am on the examination day. A person allegedly broke open several layers of trunk packaging, photographed the question paper on a mobile phone, resealed the packaging and left with it. Among those facing trial are Oasis School principal Dr Ehsanul Haque, vice-principal Imtiyaz Alam and Yadavendu. The CBI will begin presenting witnesses and evidence before the special court from Oct 1. title: Minors used to deter police action at CJPâs Mumbai protest? NHRC seeks report
text: NEW DELHI: The National Human Rights Commission ( NHRC ) on Saturday issued a notice over the alleged involvement of minors in the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest in Mumbai. The NHRC sought an Action Taken Report on allegations that minors were placed âstrategicallyâ at the protest site to deter police from taking action against demonstrators. title: âConsultancy firms, not coaching centres, at centre of NEET-MBBS scamâ
text: Dehradun : Police probing an alleged NEET-MBBS admission scam involving fake certificates to secure seats under various quotas, including the freedom fightersâ dependents quota and reserved categories, said âadmission consultancy firms, rather than coaching centres, appear to be at the centre of the racket, with no evidence emerging so far of coaching centres being involved in the scamâ. Twelve people have been arrested in connection with the case. According to officials, the claim is supported by the arrest of five accused so far by the Dehradun Policeâs Special Investigation Team (SIT). Among them, alleged mastermind Rupesh Pandit used to run an admission consultancy firm in Meerut, while his close associate Dheeraj Kumar Srivastava was running a similar firm in Bhopal. The websites of both firms claim to facilitate admissions to various courses, including medical, engineering and biotechnology. âIn our investigation into NEET-MBBS UG admissions under the freedom fightersâ dependents quota in the state, we have not found any involvement of coaching centres, unlike earlier incidents of exam paper leaks at the national level. This time, it is admission consultancy firms that were using illegal means to facilitate admissions for medical students,â an SIT officer privy to the investigation told TOI . The officer said operators of admission consultancy firms have contacts in various colleges and universities, and that both Pandit and Srivastava âknew the intricacies of the admissions processâ. âThey knew that not many students seek admission under the freedom fightersâ dependents quota. Hence, they decided to exploit this and got fake certificates and related documents issued from local administration offices,â the officer added. SP Dehradun (rural) Jaya Baluni, who is leading the SIT, said police suspect the involvement of a gang in the scam. âPandit, who was among the first two accused arrested, confessed to striking deals for Rs 45 lakh per student for MBBS admissions in Uttarakhand using fake documents. We are also probing the suspected involvement of the gang in facilitating admissions through fraudulent means in other states,â Baluni said. She added, âWe are slowly connecting the dots, with more suspects under our radar. Further arrests are likely in the coming days.â Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. title: CJP digs in heels, says will launch protest at Shivaji Park despite no nod
text: Abhijeet Dipke said if he is arrested, he âwill come again and again and againâ Mumbai: Striking a defiant note, CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke declared that the outfitâs plan to launch a nationwide protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar from Shivaji Park on Friday will go ahead as scheduled despite police refusing to grant permission for it. Police had refused the nod, citing restrictions governing gatherings at the ground. âIf Devendra Fadnavis can have a political rally at Shivaji Park, then we can protest as well,â Dipke asserted on Thursday, adding that protest is fundamentally an act of dissent and requires no permission. âDid Mahatma Gandhi have permission to protest against the British?â Taking âfull responsibilityâ for any impending police action, he told reporters, âMumbai Police is not Delhi Police. So I know it will go well.â Asked what he would do if he were to be arrested, the 31-year-old quipped, âI will come again and again and again.â Separately, CJPâs co-convener Saurav Das said if protesters are thrown into jail, they would launch a âjail theek karo andolanâ. The gathering was also reminded of the outfit having been born out of satire. Asked why CJP did not approach the judiciary for police permission to protest, Dipke quoted a popular Bollywood dialogue to indicate that such a hearing would drag on: âTareek pe tareek, tareek pe tareek.â When asked what protective measures protesters should take against potential force, he recalled that those who had protested against the NEET paper leak in Delhi had responded to police brutality with memes. âThis govt canât handle humour.â Dipke didnât spare the judiciary either. Asked about the secret behind CJPâs rapid, massive success, he said, âYou will have to ask CJI Surya Kant,â referring to remarks earlier this year that inadvertently inspired the partyâs satirical name. Dipke put forth three principal demands: a freeze on the special intensive revision of voter lists, the initiation of criminal charges against Kumar, and the mandatory inclusion of civil society members in future CEC appointments. He alleged that EVMs are ânot reliableâ. âVoting in various parts of North America and Europe is done on ballot paper. After Mumbai, CJPâs protest is set to move to Goa, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Patna, Ranchi and UP, and culminate at Jantar Mantar in Delhi at the end of the month. title: DUSU results: Gen Z protest, Satya Niketan tragedy shape poll mood; ABVP holds ground
text: ABVP rides out Gen Z protest, Satya Niketan headwinds to retain dominance NEW DELHI: The ABVP rode out the headwinds of the Gen Z protest at Jantar Mantar and the recent Satya Niketan tragedy to retain its dominance in Delhi University student politics, sweeping three of the four DUSU posts on Saturday. The result came after a campaign in which students openly discussed issues affecting them, from the NEET paper leak to the collapse of a paying guest building that claimed the lives of five DU students. The Congress's National Students' Union of India ( NSUI ), which had sought to tap into the sentiment around these issues, lost all four central posts. An NSUI rebel-turned-Independent, Deepanshu, however, won the vice-president's post, defeating ABVP's Ishu Maurya, his closest rival. The ABVP's Yash Dabas won the president's post, defeating NSUI's Vijay Shankar Meena by 2,053 votes. Riya Chhawdi and Lakshya Raj Singh won the secretary and joint secretary posts respectively. The outcome came three months after the Gen Z protest at Jantar Mantar, where the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had led an agitation seeking redressal of the NEET paper leak issue. Jantar Mantar protest shapes student discourse Ratna Singh, a CJP leader, said the protest movement had since expanded its focus to other issues concerning students and youth. "Since the Jantar Mantar protest, we have been actively addressing other issues related to students and youth, like the condition of schools in the states. The DUSU elections were a different space that we did not directly engage with," she told PTI. BJP leader Vijay Goel, who served as DUSU president during 1977-78, said the Jantar Mantar protest should not be viewed as an expression of opposition to the BJP or the Centre. "The Jantar Mantar protest was basically against the NEET paper leak issue, which the government finally addressed and resolved. You cannot say that the youth were against the BJP or the government," he said. Satya Niketan tragedy becomes DUSU campaign issue The Satya Niketan tragedy emerged as another major issue during the DUSU campaign. A paying guest building in the locality abutting DU's South Campus collapsed on September 6, killing seven people, five of them college students. The incident became a major rallying point during the campaign, with students expressing their political awareness of incidents that directly affected them. Deepanshu, who won the vice-president's post, gained popularity after he gave up wearing footwear in protest over the tragedy. Students said the impact of the Jantar Mantar protest was less about directly supporting or opposing any organisation and more about reassessing what different student outfits represented and the issues they advocated. "Students have been increasingly antagonised over the last few years. It made many of us question the positions taken by different student organisations and whether they actually represented the issues that students were raising or toed their party line," said a Hindu College student. The DUSU contest has traditionally been a direct battle between the ABVP, which is covertly supported by the BJP, and the NSUI, the Congress's student wing. While the ABVP retained three of the four posts this time, the NSUI failed to secure a place on the central panel. Congress national secretary and Karnataka co-in-charge Ajay Dutt alleged that the BJP had "influenced" the DUSU elections, as he alleged it had done in state and national polls. "Our candidate was leading for the post of president in the last rounds by around 500 votes and ultimately was declared defeated. The BJP misused the administration to influence the results," he charged. BJP leaders said the ABVP victory carried a "big message", despite Rahul Gandhi "doing his best" to "mislead and misguide" the youth. The ABVP's victory thus came despite a campaign in which recent student protests and the Satya Niketan tragedy had brought questions about student issues and representation to the forefront. The NSUI, which had dominated DUSU for a long time in its earlier years, was left without any of the four central posts. Following the report, poll panel officials said the two commissioners had raised objections to decisions taken during the electoral roll clean-up and the handling of voter databases in various states. title: Grievances, music & slogans run together at Rahul event
text: Rahul Gandhi event Rahul Gandhi in Indore Rahul Gandhi event Rahul Gandhi in Indore Rahul Gandhi event 1 2 Indore: Posters. Placards. Roses. Music loud enough to drown the afternoon traffic. By the time Saturdayâs sun began dipping over Bhanwarkuan, the road leading to Regional Park in Indore had turned into a river of young people, all headed toward IDA ground, where Congress party had set the stage for Rahul Gandhi âs âChhatron Ki Goonjâ programme. Among those making their way there was Krishi Chouhan, a student from Dhar who studies in Indore. She had gone home to Dhar on leave, but returned a day early, she said, just to be part of the event and listen to Gandhi speak. They came in numbers no one had quite planned for. Lined up on both sides of the road, students danced as speakers blared music, phones held high to capture reels for their vlogs. Young women arrived in what many described as distinctly Gen-Z style, many carrying red roses. Adhikesh Jadhav, a college student, said he had come to support Gandhi because he wanted to see him become Prime Minister one day. Looking around at the crowd swelling by the hour, he said the turnout of young people reflected their faith in Gandhiâs ideology and their frustration with the system. That enthusiasm, as the afternoon wore on, tipped into something harder to manage. By 5 pm, Gandhi had still not arrived, and the ground was already houseful. Registration windows saw such a rush that entry passes ran out entirely, leaving hundreds to seek help from local leaders and officials to get inside. Those who couldnât get in waited anyway. Inside, the crowd swelled well beyond what the dome could hold, while outside, an even larger number pressed to get in. Volunteers and attendees clashed repeatedly over gate-crashing without valid passes, and people had to be guided out through safety corridors to ease the congestion. At one point, tempers flared on the stage itself, with volunteers and police officers pushing and jostling before order was restored. To keep the restless crowd occupied, organisers turned to live music, with Indoreâs own Lushcurry, playback singer Raghav Chaitanya and their team performing hip-hop and rap. Suraksha Pathak, a bank employee who had also walked with Bharat Jodo Yatra during its Madhya Pradesh leg, said she had covered nearly five kilometres on foot to be there, pausing often through the afternoon to take photos and videos for her social media accounts. Around her, the energy from the performances grew so intense that organisers had to pause the music at several points, worried about the risk of suffocation in the packed ground, and some attendees were asked to step outside. When Gandhi eventually took the stage, he shared it with students who spoke of their own concerns â unemployment, examination paper leaks, delays by govt recruitment bodies in filling vacant posts and inadequate educational infrastructure. His remarks, woven with slideshows, touched on NEET paper leak, studentsâ future, and democracy. Young people who had travelled in from Ujjain, Dewas, Bhopal, Dhar, Barwani, Jhabua, Alirajpur, Shajapur and Ratlam found themselves part of an event where grievances, music and slogans ran together â one refrain rising above the noise: âTwinkle Twinkle little star, Rahul Gandhi Super Star.â You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Indore | Silver Rate in Indore | Bank Holidays in Indore | Public Holidays in Indore | Petrol Price in Indore | Diesel Price in Indore | CNG Price in Indore | LPG Price in Indore Stay updated with the latest Indore news. title: BJP to apprise young voters of SP govtâs âjungle rajâ
text: Lucknow: Was the previous Samajwadi Party govt as good as the present BJP dispensation? What will happen if BJP govt is replaced by SP in the 2027 Assembly elections? Will the change bring back the alleged conditions that prevailed between 2012 and 2017 when SP was in office? These are among the questions that BJP plans to toss up at the youth as it seeks to turn the memories of Akhilesh govt into an electoral narrative before the Assembly polls. BJP youth wing -- Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) -- will launch a statewide campaign in universities and colleges to âcautionâ young voters against the possibility of return to âjungle rajâ, poor law and order, and misgovernance if SP comes back to power. The campaign, tentatively titled âSarthak Yuva Samvadâ, is expected to be rolled out soon after the constitution of state and district-level teams of BJYM. It will directly engage students and first-time voters with BJP MPs, MLAs and MLCs who are expected to participate in the interactions. âA good number of youth think that the situation prevailing today also existed between 2012 and 2017. They believe that a change in govt would not alter the conditions. They need to be corrected and apprised of the reality,â UP BJYM president Rohit Mishra told TOI. The move is significant because a large section of the electorate that will vote in 2027 has little or no direct political memory of the 2012-17 SP govt. BJPâs challenge, therefore, is not merely to attack SPâs record but to make a generation of young voters relate to a period it only knows largely through political narratives. The proposed campaign is likely to be less about conventional political rallies and more about drawing a contrast between the two govts on issues that directly affect youth: crime, law and order, employment, education, and social harmony. Mishra said BJYM will present data from National Crime Records Bureau and other key indicators to show how the state witnessed a spate of caste and communal riots and how the collapse of law and order fuelled unemployment and social problems. Analysts said BJPâs strategy reflects an emerging feature of the 2027 contest: the battle over Uttar Pradesh âs political memory. For BJP, the 2012-17 SP govt represents a period that can be invoked to reinforce its core law-and-order narrative. The party has repeatedly sought to contrast Yogi govtâs governance model with the âjungle rajâ of the SP era. The challenge, however, is that younger voters may not necessarily share that memory. A voter in the 18-22 age group in 2027 would have been a child during SP govtâs 2012-2017 tenure. For such voters, BJPâs portrayal of that period will compete with SPâs narrative of its tenure, as well as with their personal experience of the current govt. This makes the proposed university and college campaign particularly significant. Instead of merely telling young voters what happened during the SP govt, BJP intends to create a forum where the past can be contrasted with their present-day concerns. Mishra said they would try to understand the youthâs expectations from the present govt and also hear their grievances. Students would be given an opportunity to voice their concerns, he said, suggesting that the campaign would combine BJPâs political messaging with an effort to gather feedback from a constituency that has become increasingly important in electoral politics. After the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest over the NEET paper leak forced education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. BJP leadership, including PM Narendra Modi and BJP national president Nitin Nabin, have been treading cautiously while reaching out to youth on various occasions. In UP, the youth-centric drive is being sharpened with Yogi Adityanath promising over 1 lakh govt jobs to them over the next six months. title: NEET protest: HC dismisses plea seeking inquiry into lathi-charge
text: New Delhi: Delhi High Court Wednesday dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking a court-monitored inquiry into allegations of a police lathi-charge on students during NEET-related protests in the capital, observing that its PIL jurisdiction could not be invoked merely on the basis of conflicting media reports. The petitioner, who described himself as a citizen and media professional, sought directions to Delhi Police to decide his representation seeking clarity on whether a lathi-charge had taken place. He argued that establishing the facts was necessary to ensure transparency and accountability. A bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia, however, questioned the maintainability of the plea and asked the petitioner to show either a legal dispute or violation of a constitutional or statutory right. Watch NEET PAPER LEAK: LESSONS FROM INDIA'S BIGGEST EXAM SCANDAL âEverything which will catch your imagination by reading newspaper becomes a PIL. High-sounding words like accountability, transparency are not to be used in vacuum... What is your petition? Delhi Police issued a statement. That statement is contradicted by the media and you are asking us to direct an inquiry,â the bench observed while dismissing the petition. The plea was filed in the backdrop of protests organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET paper leak and demands for accountability from govt, including the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan . On July 20, thousands of protesters gathered at Jantar Mantar for a âChalo Sansadâ march despite heavy security deployment. Clashes broke out after protesters attempted to march towards Parliament, leaving several protesters and police personnel injured. The petitioner had relied on what he described as contradictory accounts regarding the police response during the protest and sought judicial intervention to ascertain the facts. However, the court declined to entertain the plea, holding that such issues did not warrant invocation of its PIL jurisdiction. title: Protests against SIR, CEC: Is it time for Congress and INDIA bloc to take a leaf out of CJP's playbook?
text: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, has announced a mega action plan to take forward its campaign against âvote choriâ and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The key stakeholders of the INDIA bloc met today in the national capital to chalk out a roadmap for nationwide protests against the Election Commissionâs âflawed and partisanâ approach. The INDIA bloc's renewed offensive comes days after an Indian Express report citing internal differences within the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding the implementation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and modifications to voter registration processes. The opposition parties' meeting also comes in the backdrop of successful mobilisation programmed led by the Cockroach Janata Party against NEET paper leak, which brought the GenZ to the streets and forced the government to accept their demands. After hours long deliberations, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge unveiled the oppositionâs blueprint for intensified demonstrations against ECâs âmalpracticesâ and shared details of how the INDIA bloc will stand up against electoral irregularities. INDIA bloc's action blueprint Here is what the INDIA bloc allies decided on their action plan against ECâs âpartisan approach and malpracticesâ 'Save Democracy March' in each district from October 2 to 8 On October 6, opposition MPsâ march to Election Commission headqaurters Five rallies across India in October-November Mega rally in Delhi on November 1 to explain â vote chori â by EC Appeal to Supreme Court to expedite pending cases pertaining to SIR and other electoral malpractices Detailed presentation before President Droupadi Murmu on âcompromisedâ electoral process INDIA bloc's demands Then there was also a list of 6 demands which the opposition parties announced. It included Return to voting by ballot paper instead of EVMs Pre-SIR electoral roll for all future elections Due reasoning and effective appeal mechanism before any legitimate voter is removed from roll Protection of eligible voters from exclusion caused by administrative failures, inadequate documentation or lack of awareness Simple and accessible voter registration for our young citizens Maintaining institutional accountability and an Election Commission that commands confidence across political spectrum So far, so good. But the problem is that all these demands have already been raised by various opposition parties from time to time without any success. We have heard several leaders in the past demanding a return to ballot paper. This has not happened and is unlikely to happen. The fight over alleged discrepancies in the SIR process has been an ongoing one. We have seen Rahul Gandhi and other regional leaders raise the issue. But none of them have managed to sustain the momentum or stop the process. Even the courts have refused to back their allegations and have not stopped the SIR process. Effective action plan? Now, letâs focus on the action plan. Protests at district level, march to Election Commissionâs office, rallies, appeal in Supreme Court - all make for good optics, but can they bring about enough pressure? The Congress, which is leading the opposition block, has been consistent in raising these issues, but has failed to keep the momentum going. Rahul Gandhi has addressed several press conferences in the last two years leading the charge against the Election Commission and Gyanesh Kumar. His yatra in Bihar ahead of assembly elections last year brought the issue to centre stage but once again the momentum did not sustain. Clearly, the Congress and the other opposition parties need to think how to run a sustained campaign for mobilisation. 'Congress raises issues but fails to keep momentum going' At the CWC meeting held on Tuesday, ahead of todayâs INDIA bloc meeting, Rahul Gandhi had claimed that revelations about the Election Commission were now coming out in the open because of the Congress. During the two-and-a-half hour CWC meeting, Rahul pointed out that the Congress had been raising the "vote chori" issue strongly with facts and talked about irregularities in polls in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra but many were sceptical of it. - Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha claimed that EVM and voters' list "match-fixing" of polls was underway in the country and asserted that his party should not budge from the path of "virodh" (opposing) as well as "pratirodh" (resistance) against it from streets to Parliament. Rahul Verma, political scientist and a Fellow at New Delhi-based think tank Centre for Policy Research, feels that the Congress needs to be persistent and have patience. âOne of the reasons why the congress fails to do mobilization is that they raise important issues but are not persistent. They need to have patience. Congress has been talking about all the important issues but did not sit on a protest like the CJP,â Rahul Verma says. âEven the CJP would not have thought of the success they eventually got. They continued sitting on protest even when there was little traction in their favour. Eventually, they managed to mobilise a lot of support and forced the government to concede to their demands,â Rahul Verma adds. BJP targets opposition unity, attacks Rahul If the INDIA bloc meeting was about showcasing opposition unity, well the purpose was at best half achieved. There were more questions on INDIA blocâs united presence than answers. The BJP has aggressively highlighted the division within the opposition ranks. With several regional parties openly against the Congress, the BJP leaders have been quick to question Rahul Gandhiâs acceptance as the leader of the opposition block. - BJP national media incharge Ashish Usha Agarwal questioned Rahul Gandhiâs leadership of the INDIA bloc and said the outcomes of the INDIA bloc meeting on Wednesday were "zero vision, 100 per cent frustration. The BJP claimed that the meeting was an advance excuse for poll defeats, with the leaders of the opposition grouping rejecting Rahul Gandhi's leadership. "The INDI Alliance fell apart even before the meeting took place. The DMK did not attend the meeting. Akhilesh was busy elsewhere. The AAP had already declined," Union minister Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Shivraj Singh Chouhan said at a press conference at the BJP headquarters. âWhy is this happening? It is because the INDI Alliance is simply not willing to accept Rahul Gandhi as its leader. His leadership is not being accepted; that is why they are not even showing up," Chouhan said, contending that Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav would have come to attend the meeting if it was "really so important." Chouhan claimed that the opposition INDIA bloc is crumbling. "No matter how many times they (Congress) try to re-launch Rahul Gandhi, the INDIA bloc does not consider him their leader," he said. - Clearly, the opposition needs to do things differently. When Mamata Banerjee said the opposition had taken these matters to the Election Commission and the Supreme Court and "knocked on every possible door," it was an admission of the fact that the old ways had failed. The meeting today discussed the need for mobilisation on the ground by involving the civil society along with the political fight. title: A NEET paper leak accused in Tihar jail wants to read something unexpected: Delhi court allows Hanuman Chalisa, Shivaji Maharaj biography among other books
text: AI representation/ChatGPT What does a man accused in one of India's biggest medical entrance exam controversies choose to read while behind bars? For Dhananjay Nivrutti Lokhande, currently lodged in Delhi's Tihar Jail in the NEET-UG paper leak case, the answer is a mix of devotional texts and a book on Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. As per various media report, Lokhande approached a Delhi court seeking permission to read the Hanuman Chalisa, Mangal Stotra and âShrimaan Yogiâ, Ranjeet Desai's biographical novel on Shivaji Maharaj. The court allowed his request, subject to prison rules and security checks. According to the Organiser, the order, passed by Special Judge Ajay Gupta on September 1, allows the books to be supplied by Lokhande's family members or authorised counsel after the material is cleared according to jail procedures. Lokhande is an accused in the CBI's investigation into the alleged NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak. The agency has alleged that he was part of the chain through which the leaked examination material was moved from Maharashtra to other parts of the country. These allegations are yet to be established in court. What did Lokhande ask the court for? Dhananjay Lokhande, accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case in May. (ANI) Lokhande's application sought permission to receive the books while lodged in Tihar. The court allowed the request but placed conditions on how the material could reach him. Special Judge Ajay Gupta directed the concerned jail authorities to provide the religious books mentioned in the application, provided they were supplied by a family member or authorised counsel and cleared security checks in accordance with the Jail Manual. The decision allows Lokhande access to both devotional literature and a historical work while his criminal case continues before the special court. What the CBI has alleged against Lokhande The book request comes against the backdrop of a serious investigation into the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. According to the CBI's case, Lokhande allegedly played a key role in moving the leaked examination material from Maharashtra to other parts of the country. According to Indian Express and various media, Lokhande allegedly collected NEET examination material from Pune-based accused Manisha Waghmare and subsequently transmitted it to Shubham Khairnar. CBI had identified Lokhande as a key point in the alleged transmission chain from Maharashtra to Haryana and then Rajasthan. According to the agency's account, associates of Lokhande allegedly collected the material from Waghmare, after which it was passed to Khairnar. It was then allegedly sent onwards to Yash Yadav in Gurugram before reaching the Biwal family in Rajasthan's Sikar. These are allegations made by the investigating agency and will be tested during the legal proceedings. 22.7 lakh candidates were affected The CBI has so far arrested 13 accused in the case, according to reports. The NEET-UG 2026 examination was held on May 3, with more than 22.7 lakh candidates appearing for it, according to media reports.The NTA cancelled the examination following the alleged leak. A re-examination was subsequently conducted on June 21, with the results declared on July 16. The case has since developed into a wider investigation involving multiple people across Maharashtra, Haryana and Rajasthan. The CBI has so far arrested 13 accused in the case, according to reports. What the court's order means The permission to receive the books is limited to access to reading material. It does not amount to any finding in Lokhande's favour in the paper leak case. The books will have to pass the jail's security checks and comply with prison rules before being handed over to him. title: Caste remains a factor in DUSU polls as NSUI, ABVP break from past
text: Delhi University student union elections see NSUI field an Adivasi candidate for president (File Photo) NEW DELHI: In Delhi University , where student union elections, particularly the presidential contest, have long remained a Jat-versus-Gurjar battle, NSUI has fielded Vijay Shankar Meena, an Adivasi student from Rajasthan, for the top post this year â a move that marks a break from a pattern that has long dominated the DUSU presidency. From 2010-11 to 2025-26, every DUSU president has been a Jat or Gurjar, with the two communities also dominating ticket distribution by ABVP and NSUI. In the 13 DUSU elections held in that period, ABVP won presidentâs post nine times â while seven winners were Gurjars, two were Jats. NSUI won the presidency four times â all winners were Jats. The dominance is visible not only in who wins, but also in who gets the ticket in the first place, with Jat and Gurjar candidates repeatedly preferred for the presidency. This year, however, NSUI has picked Meena, who belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community. Originally from Rajasthan, Meena describes himself as a first-generation learner â the first in his family to pursue higher education and come to DU. He joined the university for his MA and is currently pursuing his postgraduate studies in Buddhist Studies. Both his parents are persons with disabilities and the familyâs livelihood comes from farming, with others cultivating their land. In a campaign video, Meenaâs father Ramji Lal spoke of the familyâs limited means and said they had little understanding of higher education or even what their son was studying. âMy wife and I are both disabled, so we are not able to do farming. We have given our land on rent. They take half the produce and give half to us. This is how we live. My wife also does stitching, and that is how we earn our livelihood,â he said. âNeither I nor my parents studied. He is the first in my family who studied till Class 12 in the village. In Delhi, he appeared for some examinationâ¦ We have no knowledge of education. He only told us he had got admission and wanted to go to Delhi,â he added. The visible involvement of parents in this yearâs campaign is unusual. Deepanshu Shokeen, an NSUI member from the Jat community, decided to contest the vice-presidential election as an Independent after a dispute over ticket distribution. Shokeen has also been campaigning on campus alongside his father. Meanwhile, ABVP has fielded Yash Dabas, a Jat candidate from Kanjhawala in Delhiâs rural belt, for president; Ishu Maurya, an OBC candidate from UP, for vice-president; Riya Chhawadi, a Gurjar from south Delhiâs Molarband, for secretary; and Lakshya Raj Singh, a Rajput from Rajasthanâs Shekhawati region, for joint secretary. NSUIâs panel comprises Meena for president; Vir Chatrath, a Punjabi, for vice-president; Namrata Choudhary, a Gurjar from Karawal Nagar, for secretary; and Gopal Choudhary, a Jat from Rajasthanâs Mewar region, for joint secretary. Several candidates from Rajasthan are also in the fray. Notably, the NSUI panel selection this year has faced opposition from several members and supporters within the organisation, with some like Shokeen eventually entering the contest independently after disputes over ticket distribution. Samarth Beniwal, another name linked to the NSUI camp, is in the presidential race as an Independent. Beniwal later clarified he is not in dispute with the organisation, but continues to remain in the presidential race. This yearâs fight is not a simple two-way contest. The traditional NSUI-ABVP contest is facing a challenge from the Left, which has sought to carry the energy of recent student movements into the election. The AISA-SFI alliance has fielded Ananya Raturi for president, along with candidates who have been associated with recent protests, including the one at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak. These issues have resonated strongly with sections of the youth, triggering a wider GenZ mobilisation around examination failures, unemployment and concerns over the education system. The protests eventually became part of the political pressure that preceded Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation as education minister.
