title: Sreelekha Mitra faces Calcutta HC rebuke over Modi poster, gets interim protection from arrest
text: Kolkata, Sep 3 (IANS) The Calcutta High Court on Thursday strongly criticised acclaimed Bengali actress Sreelekha Mitra for displaying a poster carrying an objectionable cartoon of Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest rally in Kolkata earlier this year, while granting her interim protection from coercive police action till December 24. The Calcutta High Court on Thursday strongly criticised acclaimed Bengali actress Sreelekha Mitra for displaying a poster carrying an objectionable cartoon of Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest rally in Kolkata earlier this year, while granting her interim protection from coercive police action till December 24. Hearing the matter, a single-judge bench of Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya described the poster as "distasteful" and said the actress' conduct had "shaken the conscience". The court observed that such offensive content should not be displayed publicly or circulated on social media, particularly by a public figure. Watch Hema Committee Report: Actress Sreelekha Mitra Accuses Malayalam Director Ranjith of S*xual Assault "Such a poster was very distasteful. Why should an established person in society hold and display such a distasteful poster that shakes the conscience? It reflects bad taste. Such offensive posts should not be made on Facebook or anywhere else. After all, she is an actress," Justice Bhattacharyya remarked. At the same time, the court directed police not to take coercive action, including arrest, against Mitra until December 24. Noting that 16 FIRs have been registered in connection with the incident, the bench ordered Anandapur Police Station to conduct a consolidated investigation after compiling all complaints filed against the actress. The judge also directed the actress to cooperate with the police in the latter's investigation in the matter. The single-judge bench, at the same time, directed the police to serve a notice 48 hours before the time of summons for interrogation in the matter. The court also directed Mitra to cooperate fully with the investigation and instructed police to provide at least 48 hours' notice before summoning her for questioning. It made clear that the interim protection could be withdrawn if she failed to cooperate with investigators. The next hearing in the matter will be on December 14. The court directed the police to submit a progress report on the investigation on that day. The controversy stems from a protest march organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in July against the alleged NEET-UG paper leak. During the rally, which witnessed clashes between protesters and police in parts of central Kolkata, Mitra was seen carrying a poster depicting an objectionable caricature of the Prime Minister. Following the incident, BJP leader Keya Ghosh lodged a complaint at Anandapur Police Station. Similar complaints were subsequently filed at the Bidhannagar Cyber Crime Police Station and several district police stations across West Bengal, with the BJP demanding the actress' immediate arrest. title: NEET protest FIRs quashed by SC: CJP hails âhistoricâ legal victory for students
text: The Supreme Court quashed FIRs against NEET-UG protesters nationwide; Ratna Singh calls the decision historic (File photo) NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) legal team lead Ratna Singh, on Tuesday, welcomed the Supreme Court's decision to quash First Information Reports (FIRs) filed across the country against protesters during the NEET UG paper leak protests, saying the legal victory was achieved through persistent advocacy. Speaking to ANI, Singh said, "Today's Supreme Court order is a historic one. We were made promises on July 25, and our legal team, along with all team members, were working hard to ensure we wouldn't back down until we received assurance on those promises.â âThat persistent effort resulted in today's Supreme Court order. From the beginning, we stated that this is a peaceful protest for the country's youth, and it will continue to be," she added. Watch NEET Centre Claims Candidate Arrived 14 Minutes Late, Submits CCTV Footage to Back Decision Singh described the quashing of the cases as a major step forward for affected youth across the country, news agency ANI reported. "This Supreme Court order will lead to the quashing of FIRs against protesters across states, bringing huge relief to students whose futures are affected by pending FIRs. We hope that not just BJP-ruled states, but all other states will also follow," he said. Another lawyer said that while the broader protest FIRs have been quashed, the court ruled that proceedings will continue against 2,873 individuals identified through facial recognition software for allegedly committing acts of violence. title: Student found dead amid hostel inquiry in Satara
text: Kolhapur: A hostel inquiry, a call to parents and the fear of consequences are among the factors police are examining after a 19-year-old college student allegedly jumped from the terrace of her hostel in Satara on Wednesday evening. Shrushti Bhanudas Birmane, a second-year food technology student of Yashwantrao Chavan Science College, was found lying in a pool of blood after falling from the terrace of the three-storey girlsâ hostel on the campus. The 19-year-old, from a village near Mahabaleshwar in Satara, died before help could reach her. Police suspect suicide, though no suicide note has yet been recovered. Police said Shrushti may have been under stress after an internal college inquiry was initiated over objectionable remarks allegedly made against the hostel rector. A senior police officer said Shrushti and another hostel resident had come under scrutiny after objectionable content targeting the rector allegedly surfaced over the past few days. âThe other girl had developed differences with the rector. During questioning, she told us that both of them (her and Shrishti) had allegedly written or put up objectionable remarks about the rector on the walls of the hostel bathroom over the past three to four days,â the officer said. The rector subsequently approached the collegeâs internal committee, which began an inquiry and contacted the parents of both students. âThe other studentâs parents reached Satara on Wednesday evening. Shrushtiâs parents, who stay farther away, had not arrived. Before they could reach, she allegedly jumped from the terrace and died on the spot,â the officer said. Police are now trying to establish whether the inquiry and the prospect of disciplinary action added to the pressure on the teenager. They, however, said the exact trigger remains unclear. The other student later told police she never imagined the matter would end in such a tragedy. College principal S T Salunkhe acknowledged that the student had appeared distressed. âShe had joined the hostel only two months ago and seemed to be under stress for some time. The college has counselling facilities for students who need support,â Salunkhe said. He said the college has decided to install safety nets around the hostel building. âAny action against individuals connected to the incident will be decided only after the police complete their investigation,â he added. The death sparked protests by members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ), who demanded accountability. âWhen NEET aspirants died after paper leak, the Union cabinet minister had to resign. Here a student has died by suicide inside the campus. We want accountability. The principal and rector should be sacked. Also, we want Rs 1 crore compensation for her the,â said ABVP office-bearer Om Malunjkar. title: First exam reforms, now 'school thik karo' campaign: How CJP is changing the discourse of politics
text: NEW DELHI: From colleges to schools. From Gen Z to Gen Alpha. From Jantar Mantar to cities and villages in states. The studentsâ protest has continued; only the stage has shifted. The Cockroach Janata Partyâs (CJP) âSchool Thik Karoâ campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. Gen Z showed the way from Jantar Mantar when they forced the NDA government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign over NEET paper leaks. Gen Alpha took the cue and brought the protests to villages and towns across states, demanding better school infrastructure and government accountability. The CJP campaign asking for school audits in villages got a huge response. The pictures and videos of schools uploaded on CJPâs X timeline exposed the sorry state of government schools across states. This was followed by ground inspections by CJP teams, which led to confrontation and a strong pushback by some state governments. Two days after the CJP launched its campaign and announced that schools in Rajasthan would be on its radar, the state education department issued new guidelines regulating the entry of outsiders, including media personnel, into government schools. Watch BCI Chief Manan Mishra Rejects CJPâs Resignation Demand, Says Lawyers Can Never Be Cockroaches Under the directives, photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live streaming involving students or school activities on campus needed prior permission from the school principal or head of the institution. The Rajasthan order went on to threaten action under applicable laws in case of any breach. So, when a CJP team went to inspect a government school on August 21, it was attacked and forcibly pushed back, allegedly by the locals. Videos of the incident showed a large number of people engaging in a heated exchange with the CJP team, pushing and shoving its members as they tried to enter the village. Some clips also showed stone-pelting and smashed windows of cars. Locals said the village did not need outside political groups to intervene in the schoolâs affairs. This perhaps became the July 20 Jantar Mantar moment (when Delhi Police used force to stop Gen Z protesters from their Sansad march) of the CJP school campaign as the violent confrontation propelled the issue to the national centre stage. School students protest in UP Meanwhile in Uttar Pradesh, Gen Alpha students of a government school staged a protest twice, in a span of four days. over shortage of subject teachers. They briefly blocked traffic also. Students of a government school in Kannauj boycotted classes and held protests against the principal for alleged caste discrimination and ordering the felling of trees inside the school campus. The students of PM Shri Composite School in Gugarapur surrounded the vehicle of the in-charge principal at the school gate as he was leaving and raised slogans against him. Protests also happened in Fatehpur, Hamirpur against lack of facilities in schools. In Hamirpur, 'Gen Alpha' children laid siege to the collectorate to demand the construction of a paved road to their school. In Unnao, hundreds of students of a government-run residential school staged a protest over alleged poor-quality food, inadequate drinking water, shortage of teachers and the behaviour of the principal, briefly disrupting traffic at a city crossing. 'Ministersâ dogs got better facilities than students' In Maharashtra, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke conducted a social audit of government-run and municipal schools in Latur district. He led a team at a Zilla Parishad school at Ujani village in Latur's Ausa tehsil. After his audit, Dipke said schools in the state were in a pitiable condition, and even "ministersâ dogs got better facilities" than students. He sought the resignation of Maharashtra school education minister Dada Bhuse. Later, Maharashtra police registered a case against the CJP convenor and others for allegedly entering a government school without permission, disrupting official work and threatening teachers. The state governments cited rules to browbeat the CJP teams away from its schools. But at the same time, they were forced to act to nullify the impact of the CJP campaign. So, while some states announced new measures to improve the condition of schools, others increased the pace of work already underway to ensure that results were seen on the ground quickly. CJP claims credit The CJP was quick to claim credit for govt actions and basked in glory. âThe impact weâve been able to make with such a small team in such a short span of time is just unreal. Multiple state governments have had to bow down. Authorities had to listen to Gen Z and Gen Alpha kids and give them their due,â it said in a post on X. âBut this does not end here. We need to keep going until even the remotest regions of the nation, even the most deprived communities, have access to the highest standard of educational facilities. They may use force, they may file cases, they may do whatever they can to crush this, but we will remain committed to the same demand,â the post read. Political parties take a cue from CJP While it can be debated whether or not the CJP campaign forced the governments into action, what can be said with certainty is that the CJP has managed to do what many political parties could not - inspire the youth to come to the streets and seek accountability from power. The two CJP campaigns also point to an interesting shift - which should be a learning lesson, especially for parties in the opposition space. We have seen the opposition parties raise the pitch against government on issues like caste and religion as these have greater potential for voter mobilisation. Rarely do we see campaigns by the opposition parties centred around health or education reforms. But that seems to have changed. Youth outreach The Congress has taken a cue and is trying to stay focused on studentsâ connect and raise issues that concern the youth. In Rajasthan, the state Congress unit is also on the streets to highlight gaps in state government school infrastructure. And itâs not just the opposition that is course-correcting; the ruling BJP has also drawn a roadmap to engage with the youth and understand their concerns. In the middle of the Gen Z protest, Prime Minister Narendra Modi debuted on Instagram and tried to communicate directly with the youth who were on the streets. The BJP has in fact formed a dedicated team to spearhead its Gen Z outreach. The team includes BJP chief Nitin Nabin, national general secretaries Smriti Irani and Vinod Tawde, Gujarat minister Harsh Sanghavi, Chhattisgarh minister OP Choudhary, along with several other leaders. The affected candidates were at iON Digital Zone iDZ Sitapura centres, Jaipur, where the examination could not be completed due to an internal power supply problem. Despite repeated efforts, the issue could not be resolved, forcing National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) to postpone the examination for the affected candidates. The health ministry has constituted a three-member committee to probe the power failure at the Jaipur centres. The panel comprises a senior Rajasthan govt official, a joint secretary-level officer from the health ministry and a chief engineer from the Central Electricity Authority. Dr Abhijat Sheth, president of NBEMS said re-examination for the 2,445 candidates will be conducted on Sept 5 at 3pm in Jaipur, with the board assuring that it will be conducted in the same manner and that the candidates' performance would not be adversely affected. "We regret the inconvenience caused to the affected candidates," he said. The nationwide examination was backed by extensive security and real-time monitoring. Around 2,527 faculty members were appointed as independent appraisers, while more than 700 senior faculty members, including deans, directors, medical superintendents and senior professors were deployed as flying squad members. Sixteen NBEMS regional command centres were operational across the country, while examination centres remained under live CCTV surveillance, monitored from the NBEMS headquarters in Dwarka. title: NTA gets 3 senior officers amid exam overhaul
text: The Centre has brought in three senior officers, including an IPS officer at NTA NEW DELHI: The Centre has brought in three senior officers, including an IPS officer, at the National Testing Agency ( NTA ), giving the embattled examination body fresh administrative muscle as it undergoes one of its biggest personnel and security overhauls following controversies over NEET-UG and UGC-NET. IPS officer Ravi Kumar Singh and IAS officer Prasanna Venkatesh V have been appointed directors at NTA, while Amit Samdariya, a 2016-batch Indian Revenue Service (Customs and Indirect Taxes) officer, will join as joint director. The appointments were cleared through separate personnel ministry orders dated August 27. The induction comes days after NTA began a wider revamp that includes removing around 600 experts from its examination panels, onboarding a fresh set of specialists and introducing a four-tier scrutiny mechanism for question papers. The agency is also strengthening examination security, recruiting additional officials and moving to new premises where security is proposed to be reinforced with CISF deployment. The measures were reviewed recently by Union education minister Pralhad Joshi as the government sought to tighten both the academic and operational ends of the examination process. NTA has been under sustained pressure since the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which triggered nationwide protests and intensified scrutiny of how high-stakes examinations are secured and administered. More recently, it was forced to order fresh UGC-NET examinations in English, commerce and sociology after multiple errors and repeated questions were detected in the June papers, adding a question-paper quality problem to its security challenges. Against this backdrop, the appointment of officers drawn from the police, administrative and revenue services marks another step in the attempt to strengthen NTA's institutional capacity. The personnel ministry has directed all three officers to take charge within three weeks. The orders state that failure to join within the stipulated period would trigger the process of debarment from the Central Staffing Scheme. The staffing changes are unfolding alongside a broader examination-reform exercise. A high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani has begun seeking suggestions from students, parents, teachers and other stakeholders on reforms to the public examination system, with the consultation open till September 13. title: MPSC paper leak row: 6, including 3 officials, arrested; candidates face fresh exam
text: Six individuals, including three MPSC officials, were arrested for the Drug Inspector exam paper leak (File photo) MUMBAI: Police on Wednesday arrested six persons, including three Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) officials, in connection with the alleged leak of the 2026 Drug Inspector (Group-B) screening examination question paper, following which the recruitment process was cancelled. The Mumbai Crime Branch arrested the accused, including an under secretary of the commission, officials said, news agency PTI reported. Six arrested in MPSC paper leak case The MPSC on Tuesday announced that it would conduct a fresh examination for the Drug Inspector Group-B posts under the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), citing the need to ensure a fair and equal opportunity for candidates and maintain the integrity and transparency of the recruitment process. As a result of the cancellation, candidates who had cleared the screening examination and appeared for interviews will also have to take the fresh examination. A total of 485 candidates had been found eligible for appointment, PTI reported. The arrested accused were identified as MPSC assistant section officers Vishweshwar Dattatraya Nakate and Gopal Bhattu Marathe, MPSC under secretary Abhijit Ganpatrao Lendwe, Kautilya Academy director Pravin Dilip Patil, and alleged co-conspirators Amrut Namdeo Patil and Lokesh alias Gaurav Rajendra Patil. How was MPSC question paper allegedly leaked? According to Crime Branch officials, the accused allegedly accessed the questions before the examination, compiled them into a separate set and circulated them among unauthorised persons, PTI reported. The case relates to the offline screening examination conducted on March 22 for Drug Inspector (Group-B) posts under the FDA. Police said the question papers had been prepared by experts under strict confidentiality protocols, but the accused allegedly breached the process and obtained the questions before the examination. A preliminary inquiry confirmed a breach of confidentiality in the MPSC examination process. Following a complaint by Mangesh Desai, a police inspector attached to the Crime Branchâs Property Cell, an FIR was registered on Tuesday. The case has been registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Maharashtra Prevention of Malpractices at Competitive Examinations Act and the Prevention of Corruption Act for alleged offences including cheating, criminal breach of trust, criminal conspiracy and corruption by public servants. The six accused were produced before a Mumbai sessions court, which remanded them to police custody until September 2. Complaints received after interview process The MPSC had earlier received complaints alleging irregularities in the screening examination. According to the commission, some candidates claimed they had received the question paper or questions before the examination and that the material was subsequently circulated through social media and other electronic platforms. The recruitment process began with an advertisement issued on July 29, 2025. The screening examination was held offline at six divisional headquarters across Maharashtra. The examination result was declared on June 12, with 506 candidates eligible for interviews. Of these, 488 candidates appeared for interviews held between July 1 and 22. The MPSC subsequently published a provisional general merit list of 488 candidates, of whom 485 were declared eligible for appointment, PTI reported. However, complaints about the screening examination were received between July 22 and 26 through emails from candidates and public representatives. The complaints alleged that some candidates had received the question paper or questions before the examination and that the material had been circulated electronically. Opposition questions paper leak, cancellation The alleged paper leak also triggered criticism from the Opposition. NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar alleged that the leaked question paper was sold to candidates for Rs 40 lakh each and demanded that the MPSC chairman take moral responsibility and resign. A BJP leader said chief minister Devendra Fadnavis had promised a thorough investigation and strict action against those found guilty. State Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal accused the government of running a âbulldozer over the dreamsâ of thousands of young people. âAfter NEET, TET, Talathi and CBSE paper leaks, now the MPSC drug inspector examination has also been found to be compromised. This is like running a bulldozer over the dreams of thousands of young people,â Sapkal said. Congress Legislature Party leader Vijay Wadettiwar said cancelling the recruitment process was a victory for candidates who had protested against the alleged leak. Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Sandeep Deshpande also questioned the timing of the police action. âWhen the government knew that the paper got leaked, why was an FIR not registered in this case immediately?â he asked.
